The provided material does not contain information regarding whether the operator is using "all the latitude" NERC allows for Part 2.3.

The material defines the latitude available under the standard, which allows the Responsible Entity to "either installs the patch or documents (either through the creation of a new or update of an existing mitigation plan) what they are going to do to mitigate the vulnerability and when they are going to do so" [csection-7d6ba196ae0e7c219624]. It also notes that "Timeframes do not have to be designated as a particular calendar day but can have event designations such as 'at next scheduled outage of at least two days duration'" [csection-7d6ba196ae0e7c219624].

While the operator's documentation describes how they utilize these options—such as adding patches "not able to be installed within 35 calendar days of evaluation" to a mitigation plan [isection-12bd999ecfa8bf61d440] and using the "Change Management Solution" to store these plans [isection-c75f69c881d6a214ff52]—there is no statement or evidence in the provided text evaluating whether the operator is maximizing the use of the flexibility provided by the standard.
